Rashi on Pesachim 51a:10:1.hebrew: הני מילי מבבל לבבל - מעיר לעיר בבבל, דכיון דלא כייפי להדדי, אם ישנה מנהגן לעיניהן יש כאן מפני המחלוקת. וכל שכן מבבל לארץ ישראל, אל ישנה את מנהג המקום מפני המחלוקת:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:10:1.english: This applies [when traveling] from Babylonia to Babylonia - [That is,] from [one] city to [another] city in Babylonia, for since they are not subordinate to one another, if he alters their custom in their presence, there is [a concern] here on account of controversy. And all the more so [when traveling] from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, he should not alter the custom of the place on account of controversy.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:10:2.hebrew: אבל מארץ ישראל לבבל - אם ישנה את המנהג בבבל, אין כאן מחלוקת, דאנן כייפינן לבני א"י, דאינהו סמיכי ובבבל לא סמיכי:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:10:2.english: However, from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia - If he changes the custom in Babylonia, there is no dispute here, for we are subordinate to the residents of Eretz Yisrael, since they are ordained and in Babylonia they are not ordained.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:10:3.hebrew: עבדינן כוותייהו - כלומר, אם באין משם לכאן, אין להם לשנות מנהגם, אלא עושין כמקומן:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:10:3.english: We act in accordance with them - That is to say, if they come from there [Eretz Yisrael] to here [Babylonia], they do not have to change their custom; rather, they act according to [the custom of] their [own] place.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:11:1.english: Even if you say [that one who goes] from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia - he should not deviate [from the local custom].

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:11:2.english: Do not eat - [the fat] of the arch [of the abomasum].

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:1.hebrew: דסרכי מילתא - של קולא, ומזלזלין יותר:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:1.english: That they extend a matter - [a matter] of leniency, and they treat [things] even more lightly.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:2.english: These people also - Since they are not learned.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:3.hebrew: סרכי מילתא - קושיא היא, דאתו לאימנועי מחלה אף מדגן:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:3.english: They extend the matter - This is an objection, [meaning] that they will come to refrain from [separating] challah even from grain.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:4.hebrew: המפריש מן האורז על הדגן — אוכל טבלים, דלא חל השם על האורז ולא ניתקן הדגן. והמפריש מן הדגן על האורז — מאכיל טבל לכהן, שאין השם חל על הדגן בשביל האורז, שהרי אינו מחוייב, ונמצא שאין זו חלה אלא טבל:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:1:4.english: One who separates [challah] from rice on behalf of grain eats tevel, because the designation [of challah] does not take effect upon the rice, and [thus] the grain has not been rectified. And one who separates [challah] from grain on behalf of rice feeds tevel to the priest, because the designation does not take effect upon the grain on account of the rice, since [the rice] is not obligated [in challah], and it turns out that this is not challah, but rather tevel.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:3:1.hebrew: רוחצין שני אחים כאחד - ואין כאן משום פריצות, דנימא מתוך שמצוין יחד ועכשיו רואין ערומים זה את זה, נותנין עין איש באחיו למשכב זכור:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:3:1.english: Two brothers may bathe together - And there is no [concern] here of licentiousness, such that we would say [that] since they are frequently together and now see each other naked, they will cast an eye, each upon his brother, for homosexual intercourse.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:3:2.hebrew: ואין רוחצין כו' - כלומר, אין נוהגים שני אחים לרחוץ כאחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:3:2.english: And [two brothers] do not bathe, etc. - That is to say, two brothers are not accustomed to bathe together.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:4:1.hebrew: קורדקיסין - אשקפונ"ש (אישקפינ"ש: נעליים קלות) רחבים, ולא חיישינן דילמא משתלפי ואתי לאייתוינהו ארבע אמות. ואין דרך בני בירי לצאת בקורדקיסין, שהן נוהגין בהן איסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:4:1.english: Kordakeisin - Wide *ashkafons* (*eschapins*: light shoes), and we are not concerned lest they slip off and one come to carry them four cubits [in the public domain]. And it is not the custom of the residents of Birei to go out with *kordakeisin*, for they treat them as prohibited.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:5:1.english: Gentiles’ stools - [Stools] on which they sell merchandise, and we are not concerned about suspicion.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:5:2.hebrew: ככותאי דמי - דכיון דלא גמירי ולאו מקום תורה הוא, סרכי מילתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:5:2.english: Like Samaritans - For since they are not learned and it is not a place of Torah, they extend the matter [to other things].

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:7:1.hebrew: מאביו וחמיו - מתוך שרואהו ונזכר שמשם יצא, נותן לבו להרהור. וכן בחמיו, נותן לבו שיצתה אשתו מכאן. וכן בבעל אחותו נמי איכא הירהורא:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:7:1.english: From his father and his father-in-law - Since he sees him and is reminded that he emerged from there, he turns his mind to [improper] thoughts. Similarly, with his father-in-law, he turns his mind [to the fact] that his wife emerged from here. And similarly, with his sister's husband as well, there are [improper] thoughts.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:7:2.english: Because of the honor of his father - For he attends to him in the bathhouse.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:8:1.english: And they came - The people of Kabul.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:8:2.english: A student may not bathe with his teacher - For he must be bashful before his honor and his awe.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:8:3.english: And if his teacher needed him - That he should serve him in the bathhouse.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:9:1.hebrew: אכל דאייתרא - חלב שבכפיפת הקיבה, שהקיבה כפופה ועשויה כקשת, ואותו חלב שבמקום היתר אוכלין בני ארץ ישראל, ובני בבל נוהגין בו איסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:9:1.english: He ate [the fat] of the bowstring [part] - [This is] the fat at the curve of the stomach, for the stomach is curved and shaped like a bow, and that fat which is in the place of the bowstring, the residents of the Land of Israel eat, while the residents of Babylonia treat it as forbidden.

Rashi on Pesachim 51a:9:2.hebrew: שוינכו ככותאי - דאמרינן לעיל: "דברים המותרים ואחרים נהגו בהן איסור, אי אתה רשאי להתירן בפניהן", ואוקמה רב חסדא בכותאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 51a:9:2.english: He rendered you like Cutheans - For we said above: "Things that are permitted, yet others have treated them as forbidden, you are not permitted to permit them in their presence," and Rav Chisda established this [as referring] to Cutheans [Samaritans].

Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:10:1.hebrew: כיון דאנן כייפינן להו וכו' - קשה לר"ת, דבפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ה.) אמר: "פשיטא, מהכא להתם מהני, דהכא שבט והתם מחוקק", משמע דבני בבל עדיפי! ותירץ: דה"מ לאפקועי ממונא, אבל לענין איסור והיתר וסמיכה — בני א"י עדיפי, שלומדים תורה ברבים, ואמרינן (ב"ב דף קנח:): "אוירא דארץ ישראל מחכים":
Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:10:1.english: Since we are subordinate to them, etc. - Rabbeinu Tam finds [this] difficult: for in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (5a), [the Gemara] says, "It is obvious [that authorization] from here to there is effective, for here is [the] 'scepter' and there is [the] 'lawgiver,'" [which] implies that the residents of Babylonia are superior! And he answered that this applies [only] to extracting money [i.e., monetary adjudication], but regarding [matters of] prohibition and permission and ordination, the residents of Eretz Yisrael are superior, because they study Torah in public, and we say (Bava Batra 158b): "The air of Eretz Yisrael makes [one] wise."

Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:10:2.hebrew: עבדינן כוותייהו - "לא עבדי כוותייהו" ה"ל למימר, ומשום פ"ק דחולין (דף יח:) נקט הכי; דקאמר התם: כי סליק רבי זירא אכל מוגרמת דרב ושמואל, ופריך: ולית ליה לרבי זירא נותנין עליו חומרי מקום וכו'? ומשני אביי: הני מילי וכו', אבל מבבל לארץ ישראל — כיון דאנן כייפינן להו, עבדינן כוותייהו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:10:2.english: We act in accordance with them - It should have said, "They do not act in accordance with them." And it used this [wording] because of [the passage in] the first chapter of Chullin (18b); for it says there: When Rabbi Zeira went up [to Eretz Yisrael], he ate [meat from] a mugremet [slaughter] of Rav and Shmuel. And [the Gemara] asks: Does Rabbi Zeira not hold [the principle that] "we impose upon him the stringencies of the place [from which he left], etc."? And Abaye answers: That applies, etc., but from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael — since we are subordinate to them, we act in accordance with them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:11:1.hebrew: רבה בר בר חנה דעתו לחזור הוה - ובחולין נמי מתרץ: רבי זירא אין דעתו לחזור הוה. קצת קשה, דהשתא לצדדין קתני: וחומרי מקום שיצא משם — בדעתו לחזור, וחומרי מקום שהלך לשם — באין דעתו לחזור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:11:1.english: Rabba bar bar Chana's intent was to return - And in Chullin as well, [the Gemara] answers: Rabbi Zeira's intent was not to return. [However,] it is somewhat difficult, for now [the Mishnah] teaches [its cases] in a disjunctive manner: "and the stringencies of the place from which he departed" — [applies] when his intent is to return; "and the stringencies of the place to which he went" — [applies] when his intent is not to return.

Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:2:1.hebrew: דילמא אתי לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב - וא"ת: והיכי אתי למיטעי? תיפוק ליה דמפריש ממין על שאין מינו! וי"ל, דבבלול איכא למיטעי, דלית ביה משום מין על שאין מינו, כדפי' בפ' כל שעה (לעיל פסחים לה.), ואיכא למיחש שתהא עיסה רובה אורז במקום אחד, ויפריש מאותו צד על צד אחר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:2:1.english: "Lest one come to separate from that which is exempt on behalf of that which is obligated" - And if you ask: How could one come to err? [Even without that,] it follows that he is separating from one species on behalf of what is not its species! And one can answer that in [the case of] a mixture there is room to err, since it does not involve [the issue of separating] from one species on behalf of what is not its species, as we explained in the chapter Kol Sha'ah (above, Pesachim 35a), and there is a concern that a dough might be mostly rice in one place and he will separate [ḥallah] from that side on behalf of the other side.

Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:3:1.hebrew: אי אתה רשאי להתירן בפניהן - תימה: א"כ, היאך התיר ר' בית שאן בפ"ק דחולין (דף ו:)? ותירץ רבינו נסים במגילת סתרים, דהאי "דברים המותרים ואחרים נהגו בהן איסור" היינו שיודעים שהן מותרים והם רוצים להחמיר על עצמן, וכן משמע לישנא "דברים המותרים"; אבל דברים שנוהגים מחמת טעות, שסבורים שהוא אסור והוא מותר, יכול להתיר בפניהם, וכן משמע בהדיא בירושלמי. וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי קאמר "דילמא אתי לאפרושי מן הפטור על החיוב", כיון דידעי שהוא פטור? וי"ל, דלאו כ"ע ידעי. וא"ת: דמשמע דווקא בבני המדינה או בכותאי אינו רשאי להתיר, אבל בפני חכמים או שלא בפניהם מותר; ואמאי, והא תנן "נותנין עליו חומרי מקום שיצא משם ושהלך לשם"? ואור"י: דמתניתין איירי במנהג חשוב שהנהיגו ע"פ ת"ח, והכא מיירי שנהגו בני המדינה מעצמם; וכן הנהו דמייתי, ודאייתרא דלקמן, קים ליה דהוי מנהג חשוב. ור"י מסתפק במנהג שאינו חשוב דיכולין להתיר בפני ת"ח: אם יכול להתיר להם, כדמשמע לקמן — ולא רצו לומר להם "מותרים אתם" משום דבני המדינה חשוב להו ככותאי, אבל לתלמידים משמע שהיו אומרים "מותרין אתם"; או דילמא יכול להתיר לעצמו בפניהם, אבל להם אינו יכול להתיר, וה"ק: לא רצה לומר להם "מותרים אתם, ומה שהחמרתם לא מחמת איסור אלא מחמת מנהג שטות", ולתלמידים היה מתיר לעצמו בפניהם, אבל לא להם. ורשב"א אומר: דלא קשה ממתני' — דרב אשי דמוקי מתני' באין דעתו לחזור, ובכותאי אפילו דעתו לחזור אסור; ולאביי דמוקי ה"מ מבבל לא"י, אבל מא"י לבבל עבדינן כוותייהו, ובכותאי אפילו מא"י לבבל אסור, והנהו נמי דמייתי הוו מא"י לבבל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 51a:3:1.english: You are not allowed to permit them in their presence - This is puzzling: if so, how did Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] permit [the produce of] Beit Shean in the first chapter of Chullin (6b)? And Rabbeinu Nissim answered in Megillat Setarim that this [rule of] "matters that are permitted, yet others treated them as prohibited" refers to where they know that they are permitted and they wish to be stringent upon themselves — and so too is implied by the wording "matters that are permitted" — whereas matters that they practice out of error, thinking that it is prohibited when it is [in fact] permitted, one may permit in their presence; and so it is explicitly implied in the Yerushalmi. And if you ask: if so, why does [the Gemara above] say "perhaps he will come to separate [challah] from that which is exempt for that which is obligated," since they know that it is exempt? One can answer that not everyone knows. And if you ask: for it is implied that specifically among the townspeople or among Samaritans one is not allowed to permit [it], whereas in the presence of Sages or not in their presence it is permitted — why [is this so], given that we learned in the Mishnah: "We place upon him the stringencies of the place from which he departed and [the stringencies of the place] to which he went"? And R. Yitzchak says that the Mishnah is dealing with an important custom that they instituted on the authority of a Torah scholar, whereas here [our Gemara] is dealing with [a case] where the townspeople adopted the practice on their own; and likewise those [cases] that [the Gemara] cites [below], as well as [the case of] de'ayitra [fat] below, it was established for him that it was an important custom. And R. Yitzchak is uncertain regarding an unimportant custom — where one is able to permit [it] in the presence of Torah scholars — whether one may permit [it] for them [the scholars], as is implied below — [since] they did not want to say to them [the townspeople] "you are permitted," because townspeople are considered to them like Samaritans, whereas to students it is implied that they would say "you are permitted" — or perhaps one may permit [it] for himself in their presence, but for them he cannot permit [it], and this is what [the Gemara] means: he did not want to say to them "you are permitted, and what you were stringent about was not due to a prohibition, rather due to a foolish custom," and to students he would permit [it] for himself in their presence, but not for them. And Rashba [R. Shimshon of Sens] says that there is no difficulty from the Mishnah: according to Rav Ashi, who establishes the Mishnah [as referring to a case] where he does not intend to return, [in the case of] Samaritans even if he intends to return it is prohibited; and according to Abaye, who establishes [the Mishnah that] this applies [when traveling] from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, whereas from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia we act in accordance with them, [in the case of] Samaritans even from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia it is prohibited — and those [cases] that [the Gemara] cites as well were from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia.
